findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the returned cleanup function
findings.body: After the disposer is called, later `message` events still invoke the stale handler. Repeated attach/dispose cycles consequently retain closures and multiply message processing. Restore `socket.off("message", handler)` to preserve the cleanup contract.

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the returned cleanup function
findings.body:
For any socket that emits `"message"` after the returned disposer is called, the handler remains active. Repeated attach/dispose cycles also accumulate listeners, causing stale or duplicate callbacks and memory leaks.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the returned cleanup function
findings.body:
Calling the disposer returned by `attach` no longer unregisters `handler`. Any subsequent `"message"` event still invokes stale handlers, and repeated attach/dispose cycles accumulate listeners, causing duplicate processing and memory leaks.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal during teardown
findings.body:
Calling the returned disposer no longer detaches the handler. In applications that use disposal when a session or authorization scope ends, subsequent attacker-controlled `"message"` events still reach the stale handler, allowing post-teardown processing under retained state or privileges.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the disposer
findings.body:
Calling the returned cleanup function now leaves the `"message"` listener attached. On long-lived sockets with repeated attach/cleanup cycles, handlers accumulate, retain captured memory, and process every subsequent message repeatedly, causing unbounded memory and CPU growth.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
